title: How Trump’s Policy Agenda Runs Through One Federal Court, in Texas
partialText: For years, conservative litigants flocked to Judge Reed O’Connor’s district. Now, North Texas has become a favorite destination of the Justice Department.

title: Deportees Sent to Liberia Recount Harrowing Details of U.S. Expulsion and Treatment by ICE
partialText: Ten deportees said they experienced or witnessed what they called abusive or violent treatment by ICE. They spent months in detention, they said, before being sent to nations where they had no ties.

title: Postal Service Rule Could Bar Millions From Voting by Mail
partialText: A judge temporarily blocked the agency from implementing a strict new rule governing mail voting. The policy could disproportionately affect Democrats and many battleground elections.

title: Ed Markey Defends Transgender Athletes in Massachusetts Senate Race
partialText: Senator Ed Markey of Massachusetts has emerged as a vocal defender of transgender rights as he tries to fend off a primary challenge from Representative Seth Moulton.

title: This Governor Could Lose His Primary. A Bridge May Be to Blame.
partialText: The closure of a crucial Rhode Island bridge for safety reasons in 2023, and the traffic nightmare that followed, have dogged Gov. Dan McKee in the Democratic primary.

title: Why the United States Can’t Quit Its Wars
partialText: The country’s longest war came to an end exactly five years ago. Today it offers lessons for policymakers seeking to avoid an endless war in Iran.

title: China Says 261 Foreigners From 23 Countries Are Missing in Tibet Flood
partialText: The disclosure offered one of the clearest pictures yet of the disaster on the Chinese side of the border, where authorities have released few details.

title: Before Nepal’s Floods, Hindu Pilgrims Sought the Divine at Mount Kailash
partialText: For many, the trek to Mount Kailash on the border of Nepal and Tibet is a once-in-a-lifetime trip to find spiritual awakening.

title: See Nepali Rescue Workers Testing Aid Delivery by Drone
partialText: Some survivors of the deadly flood and landslide have no access to food. Officials and volunteers are testing how drones can help.

title: Book Review: ‘The Disappearers,’ by Marlon James
partialText: Marlon James’s story of gay experience and murderous homophobia in Jamaica is a maximalist’s banquet — and the Booker Prize winner’s finest book yet.

title: How Marlon James Confronted ‘the Story I Was Not Allowed to Live’
partialText: With “The Disappearers,” the Booker Prize-winning author has written his most personal novel yet.

title: He Was a Top Lawn Care Influencer on YouTube. Then Everything Went Haywire.
partialText: Many people think Greg Chism is a freak — or worse. He says he was just following the incentives of the platform.

title: Who Will Rule the 2026 U.S. Open?
partialText: The players, the rivalries and the dramas to follow at this year’s tournament.

title: What Dolly Did for Tennessee Is What She Did for the World
partialText: This is what she did for the written word. And medicine. And …

title: Tennis’s Lost Shot
partialText: As the U.S. Open kicks off, we’re exploring a tennis technique that has quietly gone extinct.

title: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Telescope Leaves Earth to Chart the Stars
partialText: Astronomers will use data collected by Roman’s wide, deep gaze to study the dark universe and hunt for new worlds.
